name: William Dean Howells
credit: Photograph of William Dean Howells by Underwood & Underwood · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: William Dean Howells (1837–1920) was an American novelist, critic and editor, born at Martins Ferry, Ohio. He edited The Atlantic Monthly from 1871 to 1881, and championed literary realism in novels such as The Rise of Silas Lapham.
He began as a poet and, with John James Piatt, published Poems of Two Friends (1860); he continued to write occasional verse throughout his life.

poems.title: In August
poems.author: William Dean Howells
poems.collection: The Golden Treasury of American Songs and Lyrics (1899)
poems.text:
All the long August afternoon,
  The little drowsy stream
Whispers a melancholy tune,
As if it dreamed of June
  And whispered in its dream.

The thistles show beyond the brook
  Dust on their down and bloom,
And out of many a weed-grown nook
The aster-flowèrs look
  With eyes of tender gloom.

The silent orchard aisles are sweet
  With smell of ripening fruit.
Through the sere grass, in shy retreat,
Flutter, at coming feet,
  The robins strange and mute.

There is no wind to stir the leaves,
  The harsh leaves overhead;
Only the querulous cricket grieves,
And shrilling locust weaves
  A song of Summer dead.
